name: Raid bots: the tank holds the boss under a threat floor while a melee bot casts and a healer heals
contract: Roles act only while an encounter is active, so every bot action follows encounter_start. Classes and
spells are CoA class baselines (src/server/coa/AscensionLiveBaselineData.h): Barbarian (class 12) row {12,
0, 801576} Ancestral Strike for the tank and the melee bot, Sun Cleric (class 27) row {27, 0, 500143}
Illumination for the healer. Both are the first ranks at level 2 (AscensionSpellProgressionData.h: next
ranks 802444 at level 8 and 502421 at level 6), and the same spells drive timeline-player-casts and
sun-cleric-solar-power-resource. Client Spell.dbc (coa-dbc-viewer record against
/home/fab/CoaServer/dbc_clientset): Illumination casts in 2000 ms (SpellCastTimes 5), 40 yd range
(SpellRange 5), 30 percent base mana, 1500 ms global cooldown, no facing flag; Ancestral Strike is
instant, 35 Energy, melee range (SpellRange 2), facing required, no weapon requirement (EquippedItemClass
-1). The tank and the melee bot wield a Worn Shortsword (item_template 25, delay 1900 ms), so 20000 ms of
auto attack allows about ten swings and at least five survive the setup of the first swing. The fixture is
defensive (react state 1): it attacks only the unit that attacks it, and tanks act first each tick while
melee bots wait until the boss's victim is a tank, so the tank holds the first threat. Threat is not left
to chance: in slot run 20261025T124444474474353Z a melee bot casting Ancestral Strike took the fixture
after two swings, so the tank bot holds a threat floor (a test fixture, not threat realism): each tick it
raises its threat on the boss to 110 percent of the highest non-tank threat plus 100. The melee bot casts
its real rotation (spell_cast_count, since player casts carry no source in the timeline) and any fixture
swing at it or the healer fails the case. The tank has no regeneration, so the fixture's hits are the only
health change apart from the heals and give the healer its work; the heal assertion needs at least one hit
to bring the tank under the 90 percent threshold. All asserted values come from the harness's own
observation of native packets and the encounter timeline.
